## New

- **Add MCP servers from the terminal.** `continuous mcp add <paste-or-file>` reads what a server's README tells you to paste (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Zed, OpenCode, Codex and Devin JSON or TOML, `npx`, `uvx` and `docker run` lines, an `https://` URL, `claude mcp add` and `code --add-mcp` lines, VS Code and Cursor install links) and adds the server to your own `config.yaml`, comments kept. Nothing runs on paste.
  - It shows the exact command or URL and blocks a download run by a shell, `docker --privileged`, a mount of `/` or the Docker socket, and plain `http://` to another host. It warns about unpinned `npx`/`uvx` packages, shell wrappers, risky docker flags and keys written into the snippet.
  - It asks once before a test connection (the test runs the command), lists the server's tools, resources and prompts without calling any, marks descriptions that read like instructions, and gives a fix for a missing Node.js, uv or Docker, a timeout or a sign-in. `--dry-run` connects to nothing and writes nothing.
  - Keys go to `~/.continuous/.env` as `${{ secrets.NAME }}`; a name already in use is refused. See "Add a server from a README snippet" in the MCP docs.
  - `continuous mcp add-json <name> '<json>'` takes one server object. `continuous mcp list` shows the servers in your `config.yaml` and the project's `.continuous/mcpServers/` with secret names, never values. `continuous mcp test <name>` asks, then tests a saved server and exits `1` when it fails. `continuous mcp remove <name>` removes one and keeps its secrets. `--scope project` saves to `.continuous/mcpServers/<name>.yaml` for the project, which starts only after each person trusts the folder. The settings dialog for the same steps is a follow-up.
